title: Injunction applications - how to actually get an ex-parte order
p1: Many people think an ex-parte injunction is granted just because a situation looks urgent. But courts do not issue orders without hearing the other side unless there is a strong reason to act immediately.
p2: The surprising part? Urgency alone is not enough. The court usually looks for a clear risk of harm that cannot be repaired later. A strong application explains what may happen, why waiting is dangerous, and why immediate protection is necessary.
p3: A practical mistake many applicants make is focusing only on what the other person did wrong. A better approach is showing the court the immediate damage, supporting it with documents, and explaining why notice to the opposite party may defeat the purpose of the injunction. The first few pages of an application can decide whether the court sees a genuine emergency.
conclusion: What do you think makes an injunction application stronger: proving urgency, showing evidence, or explaining the risk of delay?
